referenceScreen.units: points on a 402-wide screen; multiply by screenWidth/402

timingRule: Creature i first starts at startDelaySeconds + i × staggerSeconds. It is visible for travelSeconds (plus pauseSeconds for crawl and drop), then hidden until repeatEverySeconds have passed since it started, and repeats.

pathSpec.across: Moves from just off one edge to just off the other in travelSeconds. Vertical position goes from startHeightPercent to endHeightPercent of screen height, plus a sine bob of wobble pt (2 cycles per crossing). Extra creatures get a small random vertical offset and are up to 25% smaller. Swerve adds two out-of-step sine waves to y (2.1 and 5.3 rad/s) and one to x (3.3 rad/s), so the flight dips and darts; the body tilts into its direction of travel, up to about 34°.
pathSpec.crawl: If dashes > 0, the trip is split into that many equal dashes: each eases forward over the first 68% of its slot and holds still for the rest (legs stop). Moves in a straight line from off one edge (at startHeightPercent) to off the other (at endHeightPercent), facing its direction of travel. At pauseAtPercent of the way along it stops for pauseSeconds with legs still. Wobble adds a small side-to-side weave.
pathSpec.drop: With several spiders, each gets its own slot across the middle spreadPercent of the width (slot order shuffled, small random jitter) and its own drop depth, spread evenly over endHeightPercent ± half of depthVarietyPercent in a shuffled order, so neighbours hang at clearly different levels. With one spider: hangs on a thread from the top at xPercent of the width. Eases down to endHeightPercent in the first half of travelSeconds, hangs for pauseSeconds with a slight bounce, then eases back up in the second half. Swings side to side by wobble pt the whole time.
pathSpec.float: Rises from startHeightPercent to endHeightPercent in travelSeconds around xPercent of the width, swaying by wobble pt. Opacity fades in and back out over the trip (sin curve).
pathSpec.fog: Fog. Each wisp sits in a lane between endHeightPercent and the bottom edge (random per wisp), drifts across the screen in travelSeconds, bobs by wobble pt (0.5 rad/s), rises about 14 pt over the trip, swells ±15% in size and ±30% in opacity over time, and fades in and out at the ends (sin curve). Use a long travel time and a stagger of about travel ÷ count so the bank is always full.
pathSpec.rise: Smoke. Each puff starts just below the bottom edge at a random x, rises with an ease-out to endHeightPercent in travelSeconds, drifting sideways by wobble pt, grows from 60% to about 220% of its size, fades in over the first 15% of its life and out over the rest. Use many puffs with a short stagger for a steady billow.
pathSpec.fall: Each piece starts at a random x across the width and falls from above the top to below the bottom in travelSeconds, swaying by wobble pt and slowly spinning. Pieces vary 70–130% in size.

creatureSpec.bat: Wings beat about 4 times a second: a quick downstroke over 38% of each beat, then a slower upstroke with the wings folded in by up to 22%. The body rises slightly on each downstroke.
creatureSpec.spider: The body and face are an image (typeu-spider-body.png, head toward the bottom). Draw the legs in code underneath it: chunky two-part legs with lighter tips, roots hidden under the body. When crawling, rotate the whole spider so its head (the bottom of the image) points in the direction of travel. When hanging on a thread, keep it upright with the thread attached to the top of the body. Shadows: light from the top-left of the screen, so shadows fall down and to the right in screen space whichever way the spider faces. Legs cast a close, fairly sharp shadow; the body casts a softer one further away because it is raised; planted feet get a small dark contact spot. On a thread the shadow is faint, soft and far away. Eight legs in two alternating groups of four. Each foot stays planted on the screen while the body moves over it, then lifts and steps forward. The stride is about 12% of the spider's size. Legs stop when the spider stops. Hanging on a thread, the legs curl in a little and wiggle slowly.
creatureSpec.ghost: The ghost is an image (typeu-ghost.png). It breathes with a slow 3.5% squash and stretch, sways and tilts gently as it rises, fades in and out over the trip, and casts a faint, soft shadow well down and to the right because it floats high above the screen.
creatureSpec.smoke: Each puff is about eight overlapping soft circles (a radial gradient from the color at 42% opacity to transparent), arranged a little differently per puff so no two look alike. A blurred cloud image or a particle system works too.
creatureSpec.fog: Each wisp is about seven long, flat, soft ellipses (radial gradients stretched 3–5x wide, the color at 34% opacity fading to transparent) plus a faint white core. A blurred fog image or a particle system works too.
creatureSpec.mote: A small glowing dot (white center fading through the color to transparent) that twinkles, its opacity varying between 10% and 100% about once a second.
creatureSpec.leaf: Falling leaves use the team's leaf artwork: seven images (five cut from the reference, plus red-toned versions of a maple and an oval leaf). Each leaf picks one at random. As it falls it rocks like a pendulum, tilting about 43° into each sway, tumbles (its width squeezes to 35% and back about every 2 seconds), and casts a faint soft shadow down and to the right.
creatureSpec.look: Cute but anatomical: big glossy eyes with highlights, pink blush, soft fur edge and a soft shadow underneath. Use the studio's drawings as the reference, or commission Lottie or 3D-rendered animation cycles that match them.

rules: Each overlay sits above its screen, full size, and never blocks touches.
It starts when the screen opens and stops at the person's first tap or scroll.
Hide every overlay when the system Reduce Motion setting is on.
Turn the whole Halloween theme on and off with one remote flag, without a release.
Show no overlay or seasonal theming for the rest of the day after a sick-day (Get Help) visit, or when the app is opened from a ketone or blood sugar reminder.
Never add overlays to protected screens, listed under protectedScreens, even if a plan seems to allow it.
protectedScreens: Every screen in the Get Help / sick-day flow, including its end screens
